provenance.note: Rows a v0.19.2 database can hold although they are not self-consistent. SQLite stores any value in any column, so an integer column can hold text; and its foreign keys are only checked when enforcement is on, so a row can refer to a task that is gone. Those two rows exist only on SQLite: the old PostgreSQL schema refuses both. users.created_by and task_collaborators.added_by have no foreign key in the old PostgreSQL schema, so their dangling values exist on both providers; the old SQLite schema declares both (ON DELETE SET NULL, db/migrations/0018_rfc036_users.sql, 0020_rfc036_task_collab.sql) without enforcing them, so on SQLite those two rows are foreign-key violations of the old database as well.

values.value: kept exactly as the old database wrote it

rows.why: §3.4 row 17 v2-source-codec: text in an integer column cannot be decoded
§3.4 row 11: the creating user was removed
§3.4 row 11b: the user who added the collaborator was removed
§3.3 旧库里本来就悬空的行: an alert of a task that is no longer in the old database
